caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular textile or fabric, possibly a sampler, prominently displayed in a vertical orientation. The textile is rendered in shades of blue ink on a light background, giving a contrast between the pattern and the base. The main body of the textile is filled with a dense, grid-like arrangement of small floral, leafy, and geometric motifs, each different from the next, primarily utilizing circular, star-like, and leafy designs. Along the left and bottom edges of the textile, there is a wide decorative border composed of a wavy line interspersed with circular floral shapes and leafy sprigs. The border is separated from the main section by a straight line. The textile has a short, fringed edge at the bottom. The drawing is presented on a beige or off-white background, and below the image are handwritten inscriptions: “Westchester County” on the lower left and “Edmond W. Brown” on the lower right.
title: Wool Coverlet
cluster: #01 — Textile Arts: Quilts, Samplers, and Embroideries
